evidence_span.text: gain or loss of Norrin/Fz4 signaling results in a cell-autonomous gain or loss, respectively, of blood retina barrier and blood brain barrier function

reviews.rationale: Genetic gain/loss experiments support Fzd4-dependent CNS endothelial barrier function, but do not test cilia assembly or any supplied gene. The adult retina/cerebellum setting only partially matches postnatal brain endothelial development.

evidence_span.text: Micro-CT scan performed at postnatal day 1 (P1) revealed random left/right symmetry dysregulation with situs inversus totalis present in most SDNme7−/− rats

reviews.rationale: Rat Nme7 knockout causally supports a ciliopathy phenotype. It does not test Smoothened localization, Hedgehog signaling, or BBSome-mediated GPCR trafficking, so support for the assigned mechanism is only partial.

evidence_span.text: The CPLANE proteins Intu, Fuz, and Wdpcp/Fritz are deeply conserved in animal evolution (Fig. 1a) and were first identified as PCP proteins in Drosophila33-37,40. In vertebrates, mutation of these genes elicits ciliogenesis defects

reviews.rationale: Gene-specific mutation evidence supports Wdpcp as a CPLANE component required for vertebrate ciliogenesis, consistent with the cilia-assembly mechanism. The experimental systems are indirect to postnatal mouse brain endothelium.

evidence_span.text: Upon detachment of the cleaved polypeptide from the N-terminal methionine, the produced L-methionine is bound to two metals (E•P), as clearly observed in the Co-Met-bound structure

reviews.rationale: MetAP1D ligand-bound structures and substrate modeling directly support cleavage of initiator methionine during mitochondrial protein maturation. The human recombinant structural system is indirect to mouse brain endothelial development.
